info.title: Telescopius RESTful API
info.description:
Request example: curl -H "Authorization: Key YOUR_API_KEY" https://api.telescopius.com/v2.2/quote-of-the-day

Response example: { "text": "You aren't in the Universe, you are the Universe.", "author": "Eckhart Tolle" }

Latest API version is 2.2

If you need new endpoints or more than 2 API keys, please contact us explaining your use case to see what we can do.

Unofficial JavaScript SDK: https://www.npmjs.com/package/telescopius-api

license.name: Commercial use not allowed unless you have prior written authorization.

get.summary: Get time information for major solar system bodies
get.description: Get time information for major solar system bodies, given a location, date and search parameters.

get.summary: Advanced search to find targets in the sky
get.description: Searches targets given a location, date and search parameters.

200.description: The total objects `matched` for this search (regardless of `results_per_page`), and the `objects` found, with their rise/transit/set times and observation at transit

get.summary: Simplified targets search, to get the most popular targets best seen around this time of the year
get.description: Get a list of popular targets for the given location and date, for which this is the best time of the year to catch them high in the sky around midnight. In other words, near opposition and with the longest time up in the night sky for you to observe or take the most subs.

200.description: The total objects `matched` for this search (regardless of `results_per_page`), and the `objects` found, with their rise/transit/set times and observation at transit

get.description: Fetch basic information about all lists for current user.

200.description: An array of simple objects, one per target list.

get.description: Returns a target list with all its targets. If order is set to rise, transit, set or next opposition, the location of the list will be used instead of the querystring parameters.
Returns all target lists belonging to the authenticated user.

200.description: An object containing an array of target lists.

get.summary: Fetch a target list by ID
get.description: Returns a target list with its targets for the authenticated user.

200.description: The target list object including its targets.

get.description: Retrieves astronomical events (eclipses, moon phases, meteor showers, planetary oppositions, conjunctions, equinoxes, solstices, and occultations) for a specified date range (7 to 365 days, default 30 days) or a specific year/month.

parameters.name: days
parameters.description: Number of days to return events for (min: 7, max: 365, default: 30)

parameters.name: date
parameters.description: Start date in ISO format or YYYY-MM-DD (defaults to current date)

parameters.name: elevation
parameters.description: Observer elevation in meters above sea level

parameters.name: max_conjunction_deg
parameters.description: Maximum angular separation in degrees for conjunctions (default: 5.0)

parameters.name: conjunction_frame
parameters.description: Conjunction frame: geocentric or topocentric (default: geocentric)

get.description: Retrieves prioritized astronomical highlights for the next 30 days (up to 10 events by default, sorted chronologically), prioritized by astronomical significance (eclipses, Saturn ring crossings, occultations, meteor showers, close conjunctions, alignments, and equinoxes/solstices).

parameters.name: date
parameters.description: Start date in YYYY-MM-DD or ISO format for date-range highlights

parameters.name: days
parameters.description: Number of days ahead to search (min: 1, max: 365, default: 30)

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of highlight events to return (min: 1, max: 50, default: 10)

parameters.name: elevation
parameters.description: Observer elevation in meters above sea level

parameters.name: max_conjunction_deg
parameters.description: Maximum angular separation in degrees for conjunctions (default: 3.0)

parameters.name: conjunction_frame
parameters.description: Conjunction calculation frame: geocentric or topocentric (default: geocentric)

get.summary: Get weather forecast for a location
get.description: The darkest sunset/sunrise are used to determine the length of the day and night. Weather information is updated every 4-6 hours so there's no need to make requests more than once every few hours. Please keep a local cache when possible.

parameters.name: include_hourly
parameters.description: Include hourly data in the response

get.summary: Get all equipment for your user
get.description: Get all equipment for your user.

parameters.name: username
parameters.description: Username of the user. If empty, it will use your username, identified by your API key.

get.summary: Get the latest news from different astronomy feeds
get.description: Get the latest news from different astronomy feeds

post.summary: Model Context Protocol (MCP) Streamable HTTP endpoint
post.description: Stateless Model Context Protocol (MCP) Streamable HTTP endpoint for AI assistants and autonomous agents. Supports JSON-RPC 2.0 requests for initialization, tool discovery, and tool execution (e.g. celestial calculations, target search, visibility, weather, user equipment, and locations). Requires an API key via Authorization header (Key <api_key> or Bearer <api_key>).

parameters.name: body
parameters.description: JSON-RPC 2.0 request payload (e.g. initialize, tools/list, or tools/call)

400.description: Bad request - Invalid JSON-RPC request or batch request.

APIKeyHeader.name: Authorization
APIKeyHeader.description: The header Authorization value should be: "Key YOUR_API_KEY"

400.description: Bad request - Usually due to invalid parameters.

401.description: Unauthorized - API key is missing, invalid or disabled.

429.description: Too Many Requests - API key has gone over the monthly requests limit.

lat.name: lat
lat.description: Latitude. [-90, 90]. Default: auto-detect from IP address.

lon.name: lon
lon.description: Longitude. [-180, 180]. Default: auto-detect from IP address.

timezone.name: timezone
timezone.description: IANA Timezone. Default: auto-detect from IP address.

datetime.name: datetime
datetime.description: Date or datetime. "YYYY-MM-DD", "YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss", or ISO 8601 string. Default: null (present time)

timestamp.name: timestamp
timestamp.description: Unix timestamp in seconds or milliseconds. Default: null (present time)

time_format.name: time_format
time_format.description: How to report times. Possible values: "24hr" or "ampm"

atmospheric_refraction.name: atmospheric_refraction
atmospheric_refraction.description: Whether to apply atmospheric refraction to rise/set times, altitudes, and ephemeris calculations. Default: true.

partner_observatory.name: partner_observatory
partner_observatory.description: The MPC code of the observatory registered on Telescopius. If provided, parameters lat, lon and timezone are ignored and used this observatory data instead.

partner_telescope.name: partner_telescope
partner_telescope.description: The code of the telescope registered on Telescopius. Please note, for this parameter to work you'll need to pass partner_observatory too.

compute_current.name: compute_current
compute_current.description: Whether to return an observation at datetime of the objects found (1) or not (0)

ephemeris.name: ephemeris
ephemeris.description: Set to 'daily' or 'yearly' if you want to calculate the ephemeris for the given day or the upcoming 12 months respectively. WARNING: only works when `name` and `name_exact` are set (in other words, when searching for a single target).

ephemeris_hour.name: ephemeris_hour
ephemeris_hour.description: A decimal hour that will be used when computing the yearly ephemeris.

sp_types.name: types
sp_types.description: Object types. You can enter multiple DSO type IDs separated by a comma. Possible values: COMET, ASTEROID, DEEP_SKY_OBJECT, GXY, etc.

sp_name.name: name
sp_name.description: Find objects by name. This performs a fuzzy search and forces the `order` to be by name match score.

sp_name_exact.name: name_exact
sp_name_exact.description: Whether to filter by exact name match or impartial matches.

sp_con.name: con
sp_con.description: Constellations. You can enter multiple values separated by a comma. IAU abbreviations.

sp_comet_orbit.name: comet_orbit
sp_comet_orbit.description: Type of comet orbit. You can enter multiple values separated by a comma. Possible values: PERIODIC, NON_PERIODIC, ASTEROIDAL, INTERSTELLAR

sp_hour_min.name: hour_min
sp_hour_min.description: The minimum hour of your observing session. Default: "sunrise". Possible values: numbers [0, 24), or the strings "sunrise", "sunset", "civil_sunrise", "civil_sunset", "nautical_sunrise", "nautical_sunset", "astronomical_sunrise", "astronomical_sunset", "darkest_sunrise", "darkest_sunset"

sp_hour_max.name: hour_max
sp_hour_max.description: The maximum hour of your observing session. Default: "sunrise". Possible values: numbers [0, 24), or the strings "sunrise", "sunset", "civil_sunrise", "civil_sunset", "nautical_sunrise", "nautical_sunset", "astronomical_sunrise", "astronomical_sunset", "darkest_sunrise", "darkest_sunset"

sp_min_alt.name: min_alt
sp_min_alt.description: The minimum altitude in the sky the objects need to reach to be reported. Possible values: [0-90].

sp_min_alt_minutes.name: min_alt_minutes
sp_min_alt_minutes.description: The minimum amount of minutes the objects need to spend above `min_alt` to be reported. Min: 1, Max: 1440. Value 0 is invalid.

sp_az_quadrants.name: az_quadrants
sp_az_quadrants.description: Limit AZ quadrants you have in view. Possible values: NE, NW, SW, SE. You can enter multiple values separated by a comma.

sp_moon_dist_min.name: moon_dist_min
sp_moon_dist_min.description: The minimum distance between the Moon and the objects at transit time. You can also pass these special values that will dynamically calculate the distance to the moon using a moon-avoidance Lorentzian depending on the selected date and the type of astrophotography you wan to do: narrowband, ha_s2, o3, lrgb

sp_moon_dist_max.name: moon_dist_max
sp_moon_dist_max.description: The maximum distance between the Moon and the objects at transit time to be reported.

sp_ra_min.name: ra_min
sp_ra_min.description: Minimum Right Ascension at transit time. [0, 24]

sp_ra_max.name: ra_max
sp_ra_max.description: Maximum Right Ascension at transit time. [0, 24]

sp_mag_unknown.name: mag_unknown
sp_mag_unknown.description: Wether to return objects with unknown apparent magnitudes or not. Default: 1 (true)

sp_order.name: order
sp_order.description: How to sort the results. Possible values: "name", "con", "dec", "mag", "ra", "rise", "set", "transit", "size", "subr", "type", "imaging_time". For DSOs, you may also use "popularity" and "opposition".

sp_order_asc.name: order_asc
sp_order_asc.description: Whether to use ascending order or not. Default: 1

sp_results_per_page.name: results_per_page
sp_results_per_page.description: How many results to show per request. Possible values: [1-120]

sp_page.name: page
sp_page.description: Which page to show for this request. The number of available pages depend on the `matched` result and the `results_per_page`. If you request a page beyond the limit, an empty result set will be returned.

sp_size_unknown.name: size_unknown
sp_size_unknown.description: Wether to return objects with unknown apparent sizes or not. Default: 1 (true)

sp_subr_unknown.name: subr_unknown
sp_subr_unknown.description: Wether to return objects with unknown surface brightnesss or not. Default: 1 (true)

sp_cat.name: cat
sp_cat.description: Catalogs. You can enter multiple catalog acronyms separated by a comma.

sp_center_ra.name: center_ra
sp_center_ra.description: Used together with center_dec and one or both of dist_min and dist_max, this is used to find objects at the given distances from the given center point.

sp_center_dec.name: center_dec
sp_center_dec.description: Used together with center_ra and one or both of dist_min and dist_max, this is used to find objects at the given distances from the given center point.

sp_dist_min.name: dist_min
sp_dist_min.description: Used together with center_ra and center_dec, used to return objects at least this distance from the given center point. Value in degrees.

sp_dist_max.name: dist_max
sp_dist_max.description: Used together with center_ra and center_dec, used to return objects at most this distance from the given center point. Value in degrees.
